milestone: Milestone 4: Scientific Communication: Paper and Talk

entries.objective: Prepare the final paper structure by integrating the first three milestones.
entries.prompt: I am preparing Milestone 4 for my seminar topic, List-Based Scheduling for High-Level Synthesis. I already have the first three milestones: technical understanding, scientific context, and critical evaluation. Now I need help organizing them into a final paper structure that communicates the topic clearly and keeps facts, interpretation, and critique separate.
entries.ai_output_summary: The AI helped organize the final paper into sections covering introduction, background, list-based scheduling method, example, scientific context, critical evaluation, embedded-system relevance, conclusion, and AI usage protocol.

actions: Checked that the final paper structure integrates Milestones 1, 2, and 3 instead of starting independently.
Checked that the structure includes technical explanation, context, critical evaluation, and conclusion.
Checked that the student name and ID are included correctly in the milestone and protocol files.

issues: The final paper structure still needs to be adapted to the exact course template if the professor provides one.
The final paper should include actual implementation figures or screenshots if available.
The corrected version explicitly includes Student ID 2220070 in all files.

integration.section: Proposed Final Paper Structure; Integration of Previous Milestones

entries.reflection: This helped me see how the previous milestones can become one coherent final paper instead of separate disconnected parts.

entries.objective: Prepare a presentation plan that explains the topic visually and clearly.
entries.prompt: For the same Milestone 4, I also need a talk or presentation plan. I do not want the slides to be a text-heavy copy of the paper. I want a clear slide structure that explains the motivation, the scheduling idea, the small example, tradeoffs, strengths, limitations, and final judgment.
entries.ai_output_summary: The AI prepared a slide-by-slide presentation plan with motivation, HLS flow, scheduling problem, DFG example, list-based scheduling concept, schedules for one ALU and two ALUs, tradeoff, related approaches, strengths, limitations, embedded-system relevance, conclusion, and discussion questions.

actions: Checked that the slides focus on explanation and discussion rather than copying paper text.
Checked that the slide plan includes examples, diagrams, formal sketches, tradeoffs, and critical judgment.
Checked that the example is consistent with the earlier milestones.

issues: Actual slide design and figures still need to be created separately.
The talk length should be adjusted to the time limit given by the lecturer.

integration.section: Proposed Slide Structure; Suggested Visuals and Diagrams

entries.reflection: This made the presentation easier to plan because the slides now follow a clear explanation path from motivation to conclusion.

entries.objective: Develop clear opening, closing, and discussion questions for the presentation.
entries.prompt: I want to make the presentation easier to deliver. Please help me prepare a natural opening, a short conclusion, and some discussion questions for the audience. The language should sound like a student presenting the topic, not like a generated final essay.
entries.ai_output_summary: The AI helped draft a short natural talk opening, a closing statement, and discussion questions about priority rules, multi-cycle operations, memory constraints, exact methods, and FPGA timing validation.

actions: Checked that the opening introduces HLS and scheduling clearly.
Checked that the closing contains both the usefulness and limitation of list-based scheduling.
Checked that the discussion questions connect to the critical evaluation from Milestone 3.

issues: The student should practice the talk and adjust wording to sound natural in their own speaking style.
The discussion questions can be reduced if the presentation time is short.

integration.section: Talk Opening; Talk Closing; Discussion Questions

entries.reflection: The opening and closing help me present the topic more confidently and keep the talk focused.
